**Mode:** a review of a fixed range, read-only. I checked each finding against the code myself. I did not run the paired validator and refuter agents, so the findings are **not independently adjudicated and not scored**. Treat this as a draft review.

**Scope:** 3 files, +184 −58 · base `7e291b7` → HEAD `61eec18` (1 commit: *refactor(mobile): extract shared address-scan logic into useScannedAddressToSend*)
**Profile:** Safe{Wallet} monorepo · the mobile app (Expo, TypeScript, Jest) · rules from `AGENTS.md` and `apps/mobile/AGENTS.md` · security, performance and architecture had nothing relevant to check.

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **OK to open the PR.** Nothing blocks it. |
| Behaviour change | None. `onScan` still warns about a chain mismatch, sets `hasScanned`, turns the camera off and calls `dismissTo` in the same order as before. The toast dedup set is still per scanner instance (`useRef`). |
| What to fix first | F1: either remove the unused `replace` mode or wire up the header scanner in this PR. |
| Score | None. Nothing was independently adjudicated (0 of 4 findings). |

## Findings

| ID | Pri | Area | Where | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | P3 | KISS / misleading comment | `apps/mobile/src/features/Send/hooks/useScannedAddressToSend.ts:22` (also `:20`, `:57-59`, `:61`, `:67`) | The doc comment says the hook is shared with the header scanner (`/wallet-connect-scan`), and `NavigateMode`/`'replace'` exist only for that scanner. Nothing in this diff or the repo uses it: `ScanConnect` → `WalletConnectScan.container` → `useWalletConnectScan` never imports the hook. So the `replace` branch has no production caller, and the comment describes something that isn't true at HEAD. **Fix:** keep only `dismissTo` and a comment about one scanner until the header-scanner PR lands, or add that integration here. |
| F2 | P3 | Testing | `apps/mobile/src/features/Send/ScanQrSend.container.tsx:57-77` | The rewritten `onScan` has no test. Nothing covers invalid code → toast, valid code → warn and navigate, the ignored second scan (`hasScanned` guard), or the empty codes array. If you revert the container change, no test fails. The hook tests only cover the hook's parts separately. **Fix:** add a container test that mocks `QrCamera`'s `onScan` and checks the guard and the order of calls. |
| F3 | P3 | Testing | `apps/mobile/src/features/Send/hooks/useScannedAddressToSend.test.tsx:91-98` | The "once per value" test only checks that the same value is shown once. A bug that dedups *every* value (a single boolean flag) would still pass. **Fix:** call it again with `'bar'` and expect 2 calls. |
| F4 | P3 | Conventions | `apps/mobile/src/features/Send/hooks/useScannedAddressToSend.ts:11-14, 22-25, 57-59` | Three comment blocks (11 lines) in a 77-line file. `AGENTS.md` says to "treat code comments as tech debt… add them only when really necessary". The `dismissTo` vs `replace` note is worth keeping if F1 keeps `replace`. The others repeat what the names and types already say. **Fix:** cut them to what isn't obvious from the code. |

## Worth tidying (no score impact)

1. `apps/mobile/src/features/ImportReadOnly/hooks/useScan/index.ts:38-55` re-implements the same parse, validate and "toast once per value" logic. It keeps the dedup set in a **module-level** `toastForValueShown` object, so it never resets across mounts. It could use `resolveScannedAddress` and a per-instance ref like the new hook. This is about 10 lines and fits the pattern this PR introduces.

## Not sure about / not checked

- I didn't run tests or type-check, as you asked. The test mocks all of `expo-router` with only `useRouter`. That's fine if `@/src/tests/test-utils`' `renderHook` doesn't need other `expo-router` exports, but I didn't confirm it.
- Ruled out: a regression risk from moving `hasScanned` and `setIsCameraActive` out of `navigateToRecipient`. The order is the same and there is only one caller.
- The architecture concern that `WalletConnect` would later import from `Send/hooks` (reaching into another feature's internals) is outside this diff, so I didn't file it.

Your call on the tidy-up: **fix**, **ticket**, or **skip**. If you don't answer, I'll treat it as skip. I haven't changed any files.
